chunks: And in the narration of 'Ammār also:

That he gives the midwife a quarter of it; and if there is no midwife, then it is for his mother—she may give it to whomever she wishes. And she should feed from it ten Muslims, and if he gives more, then it is better.

key_terms.أُمِّهِ: his mother, who may distribute the share if no midwife is present
key_terms.الْقَابِلَةَ: the midwife who receives a designated share
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: Muslims who are fed from the 'aqiqah
key_terms.رُبُعَهَا: a quarter of it, meaning a fourth share of the 'aqiqah
key_terms.عَشَرَةً: ten, referring to the number of Muslims to be fed
key_terms.عَمَّارٍ: the narrator 'Ammār in whose report this wording appears

ai.seo_question: How should the 'aqiqah be distributed if there is a midwife or if there is none?
ai.summary: This hadith gives rulings related to distributing the 'aqiqah meat. It states that a quarter is given to the midwife, and if there is no midwife, the mother may distribute that share as she wishes. It also recommends feeding ten Muslims from it, with feeding more described as better.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4718 - In another narration from Ammar, it is reported:

"A quarter of the Aqiqah should be given to the midwife. If there is no midwife, then the child's mother may give it to whomever she wishes. She should also feed ten Muslims from it, and if she feeds more, it is even better."
